sourceNote: Curated, non-overlapping year bands (inclusive) for rough coeval context only — not relationships to any Lane person.

figures.label: John Winthrop
figures.blurb: Bay Colony leader and early Massachusetts governorship, emblematic of Puritan New England in the 17th century.

figures.label: Cotton Mather
figures.blurb: Minister and writer associated with late colonial Boston intellectual and religious life.

figures.label: Jonathan Edwards
figures.blurb: Theologian and revival figure of the First Great Awakening in colonial America.

figures.label: Benjamin Franklin
figures.blurb: Printer, scientist, and statesman from Philadelphia bridging colonial politics and the Revolutionary era.

figures.label: Paul Revere
figures.blurb: Artisan and patriot whose midnight ride in 1775 is a familiar Revolutionary War touchstone in Massachusetts.

figures.label: Alexander Hamilton
figures.blurb: First Secretary of the Treasury; deeply involved in the Federalist shaping of the early U.S. government.

figures.label: Sacagawea
figures.blurb: Lemhi Shoshone guide on the 1804–06 Lewis and Clark expedition across the Louisiana Purchase west.

figures.label: Sojourner Truth
figures.blurb: Abolitionist and women’s rights speaker whose public ministry began after escaping enslavement in New York State.

figures.label: Elizabeth Cady Stanton
figures.blurb: Suffrage advocate and drafter of the 1848 Seneca Falls Declaration of Sentiments in New York.

figures.label: W. E. B. Du Bois
figures.blurb: Sociologist and civil rights leader; co-founder of the NAACP and a voice of the post-Reconstruction and Progressive eras.

figures.label: Eleanor Roosevelt
figures.blurb: First Lady, diplomat, and UN human-rights work tied to the mid-20th century United States.

figures.label: Thurgood Marshall
figures.blurb: Civil rights attorney and later the first Black justice on the U.S. Supreme Court (Brown v. Board era to late century).

figures.label: Barbara Jordan
figures.blurb: Civil rights–era U.S. representative from Texas; noted for 1974 remarks on the Constitution and impeachment.

figures.label: Sonia Sotomayor
figures.blurb: U.S. Supreme Court justice whose appointment in 2009 continued trends toward a more demographically open federal bench.
